skill.description: Edit existing images with Google Nano Banana 2 through the RunComfy CLI. Request background changes, localized edits, and reference-guided variations with configurable output settings.
skill.summary: Guide targeted image edits through RunComfy with preservation instructions, spatial prompts, and multiple image references.
skill.author: prime-skills

security_audit.summary: All 49 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, illustrative URLs, expected authentication, documented service operations, or model routing. One semantic finding identifies conditional shell injection if user text is inserted into the examples without shell-safe argument handling. No evidence found of malicious prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or reconnaissance; the external CLI implementation was not available for verification.

remediation.issue: The examples use single-quoted shell arguments, but the safety claim does not account for unsafe insertion of user text.
remediation.suggestion: Serialize inputs with a JSON library and invoke the CLI using an argument array without a shell. Explain that JSON escaping alone does not provide shell escaping.

semantic_findings.title: Conditional Shell Injection in Adapted Command Examples
semantic_findings.description: Examples wrap JSON in single-quoted shell arguments. Inserting user text containing an apostrophe without shell escaping can break quoting and permit command execution. The claim "No shell injection surface from prompt content" overlooks shell parsing before CLI execution.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The examples and unconditional safety claim directly support a guidance defect. Exploitation requires unsafe user-text insertion; no vulnerable interpolation implementation is included.

content.user_title: Edit Images with Nano Banana 2 on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Image edits can unintentionally alter subjects, branding, or composition. This skill structures preservation-focused requests and invokes Nano Banana 2 through the RunComfy CLI.
actual_capabilities: Submit image-edit requests to the google/nano-banana-2/edit endpoint through the RunComfy CLI.
Structure preservation instructions for identity, pose, clothing, branding, and framing.
Describe localized changes using spatial instructions for backgrounds, objects, and label text.
Provide 1 to 20 input image URLs, with the first image primary and remaining images supplying auxiliary cues.
Configure 1 to 4 outputs, seed, aspect ratio, resolution, output format, safety tolerance, generation limits, and optional web search.
Download generated results to a selected output directory through the CLI.
limitations: Requires an installed RunComfy CLI, authenticated account, and publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs; processing is remote.
Accepts at most 20 inputs and produces at most 4 outputs; one output per input is not guaranteed.
Complex edits can drift, and exact identity or text preservation is not guaranteed.
Multilingual image text may need another model; optional web search adds cost and latency. External CLI security claims were not independently verified.

use_cases.title: Refresh Product Backgrounds
use_cases.description: Request consistent studio backgrounds while preserving product appearance and framing across separate edits.

use_cases.title: Update Portrait Settings
use_cases.description: Change a portrait background while specifying that identity, clothing, and pose must remain unchanged.

use_cases.title: Create Controlled Visual Variants
use_cases.description: Request localized object changes and compare variants using consistent prompts, output dimensions, and seed settings.

prompt_templates.title: Replace a Background
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [image URL] with Nano Banana Edit. Keep the subject identity, pose, and clothing unchanged. Replace only the background with [setting].

prompt_templates.title: Make a Localized Edit
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [image URL] with Nano Banana Edit. Keep the composition, lighting, and other objects unchanged. Remove only [object] in [location].

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Product Images
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit for each approved product URL in [list], in separate calls. Preserve product appearance. Apply [background], square framing, and 1K resolution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: maintain consistent settings across multiple product edits.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Reference-Guided Variants
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Nano Banana Edit with [primary URL] and [reference URLs]. Preserve [details]; change only [region]. Request four 2K PNG variants with seed [seed].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: guide variants with multiple references and explicit generation settings.

output_examples.input: Replace a portrait background with a rainy street while preserving the person.
output_examples.output: Illustrative result: an edited portrait with a rainy street background and the requested identity, pose, and clothing preserved.

output_examples.input: Remove the leftmost object from a still life while keeping the remaining scene unchanged.
output_examples.output: Illustrative result: the leftmost object is removed while the other objects, table, and lighting remain consistent.

output_examples.input: Prepare three product images with matching studio backgrounds and square framing through separate calls.
output_examples.output: Illustrative result: three edited product images with consistent backgrounds and framing, saved to the selected output directory.

best_practices: State preservation goals first, then request one spatially precise change.
Keep aspect ratio and resolution consistent across related edits, and inspect results for unintended changes.
Use only images approved for remote processing, and pass serialized JSON as a CLI argument without shell interpolation.
anti_patterns: Combining many unrelated changes in one prompt.
Treating 20 reference inputs as a guarantee of 20 separate outputs.
Uploading confidential images or pasting authentication tokens into prompts.

faq.question: What do I need before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI, authenticate through login or RUNCOMFY_TOKEN, and provide publicly fetchable HTTPS image URLs.

faq.question: Does image processing happen locally?
faq.answer: No. The CLI submits requests to RunComfy, where model servers fetch the image URLs and perform remote processing.

faq.question: How many input and output images are supported?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint accepts 1 to 20 inputs and returns 1 to 4 outputs. Additional inputs provide auxiliary cues.

faq.question: Can I control output size and format?
faq.answer: Yes. Documented resolutions range from 0.5K to 4K, with configurable aspect ratios and PNG, JPEG, or WebP output.

faq.question: Will every edit preserve identity and text exactly?
faq.answer: No. Preservation prompts guide the model but cannot guarantee exact results. The skill recommends another model for multilingual image text.

faq.question: Can this skill generate images without an input image?
faq.answer: No. This skill targets image editing. Its routing guidance points to Nano Banana 2 text-to-image for generation without reference images.
